title: Enhancing Uptake of Needle and Syringe Programs in Canadian Federal Prisons
official: Enhancing Uptake of Needle and Syringe Programs in Canadian Federal Prisons
summary: This study is focused on improving the implementation of Prison Needle Exchange Programs (PNEPs) in Canadian federal prisons, with the goal of increasing the uptake of these programs among people who inject drugs in prison. The study is being conducted in nine federal prisons, including five women's prisons, where a higher proportion of incarcerated individuals report a history of injection drug use. This study aims to improve PNEP adoption and sustainability by identifying barriers and facilitators and implementing evidence-based strategies to enhance program engagement.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* All people incarcerated at a study site during the intervention period

Exclusion Criteria:

\- None (site level intervention)
sponsor: McGill University Health Centre/Research Institute of the McGill University Health Centre
